stories.title: Sources: NFL expected to suspend Rams' Alaric Jackson for two games for punch
stories.summary: The NFL is expected to suspend Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games without pay, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
stories.detail: LOS ANGELES -- The NFL is expected to suspend Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games without pay after he punched Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb following Monday night's game, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter. The NFL has not yet notified the Rams or the NFL Players Association, however, the sources told Schefter. Barring a successful appeal, Jackson will miss the Rams' games against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6 and the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7. In a scene captured by ESPN's cameras, Jackson stood near midfield following Monday's contest while exchanging jerseys with Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker when it appeared Chubb said something to Jackson. Jackson then walked toward Chubb before punching Chubb in the face with his right hand. "It's just emotions, you know what I mean? Emotional game. It was a close game," Chubb told the California Post in Buffalo's locker room. "And, you know, they always catch the second guy. So, I let him swing. And then my teammates held me back, and I just chilled." Jackson was pulled away by Rams tight end Colby Parkinson after the punch. "Like I said, it was emotional game. Tempers got flared," Chubb said. "But it i…

stories.title: Bears DE Montez Sweat suspended two games for violating NFL's PED policy
stories.summary: The NFL has issued a two-game suspension to Bears defensive end Montez Sweat for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing substances.
stories.detail: Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat has been suspended for two games without pay for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing substances. Sweat, 30, will miss the Bears' Week 6 matchup at the Atlanta Falcons and Week 7 against the New England Patriots . He will be eligible for reinstatement on Friday, Oct. 23. Sweat's suspension comes two days after fellow Bears defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo exited the first half of Chicago's 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers with a quad injury and did not return. Coach Ben Johnson did not have an update on Odeyingbo's health Monday. Sweat has totaled seven tackles and two sacks over Chicago's first five games of the season. He led the Bears with 10 sacks last season. The Bears activated defensive end Shemar Turner off the physically unable to perform list Tuesday. Turner, a former second-round pick, has been back at practice since Sept. 23 and will take Sweat's spot on the 53-man roster. Turner was limited to five games during his rookie season and suffered a season-ending ACL tear on Oct. 26, 2025. He provides depth to a thin group at defensive end led by Austin Booker , who has a team-high four sacks. "I think with any of the…

stories.summary: Elijah Culp joins cornerback Domani Jackson on Green Bay’s practice squad
stories.detail: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Green Bay Packers announced on Tuesday that the team signed cornerback Elijah Culp, whom the team brought in on Monday for a tryout . There’s little info out there about Culp, but here’s what we wrote on him yesterday: Culp is an undrafted rookie who played for four different college programs over six seasons (Austin Peay, Troy, Charlotte and James Madison). He originally signed with the Arizona Cardinals, coached by Matt LaFleur’s brother, before signing with the Indianapolis Colts’ practice squad in late September. He was released by the Colts last week and previously had a workout with the New York Giants prior to signing with Indianapolis. Worth noting: Culp’s defensive coordinator in Arizona is Nick Rallis, who also served as the defensive coordinator under then-head coach Jonathan Gannon, now the Packers’ defensive coordinator. It’s possible that he has familiarity with the scheme. Green Bay decided to release guard Josh Gesky to make room for the addition of Culp. stories.title: Sources: Rams release kicker Mevis after miscues in loss, sign Grupe from Jets
stories.summary: The Rams are releasing kicker Harrison Mevis and signing Blake Grupe off the Jets' practice squad, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo on Tuesday.
stories.detail: LOS ANGELES -- The Rams are releasing kicker Harrison Mevis and signing Blake Grupe off the New York Jets ' practice squad, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo on Tuesday. The change comes after Mevis missed a 50-yard field goal attempt in the first quarter and had a 48-yard kick blocked in overtime that would have been the winner in Monday night's 37-34 loss to the Buffalo Bills . After the game, Rams coach Sean McVay said he would "evaluate everything" about the kicking unit. "In the kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal, not even close to good enough," McVay said. "It cost us the game tonight." The Rams have had three blocked field goal attempts since the start of last season, tied for the most in the NFL, according to ESPN Research. Los Angeles has had 81 missed or blocked kicks under McVay (since 2017, including playoffs), which is third most in the league. Mevis was 5-for-9 on field goal attempts this season. Grupe started last season with the New Orleans Saints , going 18 of 26 on field goal attempts. stories.detail: The NFL has suspended Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson two games, without pay, for punching Buffalo Bills pass rusher Bradley Chubb following Monday night’s game between the two teams, according to a new report from Aaron Wilson . After a chaotic game saw the Bills defeat the Rams by a final score of 37-34, players from both teams were gathering at midfield for the traditional post-game handshakes and jersey exchanges. Nearby, Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen was conducting an interview. But in the middle of it all a verbal exchange between Jackson and Chubb turned heated, and after Chubb initially walked away from Jackson, the Rams offensive lineman confronted him and then connected with Chubb on a quick right to the jaw that came seemingly out of nowhere. stories.title: Steelers Week 5 grades: Offense has most complete performance of the year
stories.summary: Steelers Week 5 grades.
stories.detail: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Don’t look now, but the Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense is getting hot. They scored a season-high 34 points against the Indianapolis Colts, and are averaging just over 30 points over their last three games. As we do each week, Joey Bray and I will hand out grades for the previous game’s performances, so let’s get into it. QB Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers put up another solid performance against the Colts, finishing the day going 22-of-31 for 235 yards and three touchdowns. This marked his third straight game with three or more touchdown passes, tying a franchise record held by Terry Bradshaw and Ben Roethlisberger. He was decisive, he used the entire field, and he protected the ball – you can’t ask for much more than that. Grade: A- Joey Bray: Rodgers started this game with 11 consecutive completions. This game also marked the first time since December of 2021 that Rodgers has thrown for three or more touchdown passes in three consecutive contests. stories.title: Browns place Raheim Sanders on IR, sign Audric Estime off Vikings practice squad
stories.summary: The Browns have made a couple of moves at running back and on the practice squad.
stories.detail: The Browns have made a couple of moves at running back and on the practice squad. Cleveland announced the club has placed running back Raheim Sanders (hip) on injured reserve. As a corresponding move, the club has signed running back Audric Estime to the 53-man roster off of Minnesota’s practice squad. Sanders was injured in Sunday’s loss to the Jets. He served as the primary kick returner for Cleveland, averaging 29.3 yards per return. Estime appeared in seven games with one start for New Orleans last year, rushing for 198 yards with a touchdown. He caught 12 passes for 103 yards. He previously appeared in 13 games for Denver in 2024. Additionally, Cleveland signed tight end Devin Culp and guard Vershon Lee to the practice squad and released cornerback Myles Bryant and receiver James Proche II from the practice squad.

stories.title: Celtics to extend guard Payton Pritchard on 2-year, $44.2M deal
stories.summary: Celtics guard Payton Pritchard has agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million extension with a mutual option for the 2029-30 season.
stories.detail: Boston Celtics guard Payton Pritchard has agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension, plus a mutual option in the 2029-30 season, CAA co-head of basketball Austin Brown and agent Max Saidman told ESPN on Tuesday. Pritchard -- the 2024 NBA champion and 2025 Sixth Man of the Year -- cashes in on a fully guaranteed two-year max extension to keep him a key long-term member of the retooled Celtics after the 6-foot-1 guard averaged career highs in points (17), assists (5.2) and rebounds (3.9) last season. The deal keeps Pritchard for an additional season after his current deal ends in 2028. Pritchard will be set to make over $21 million for the 2028-29 season before a mutual option in 2029-30 worth nearly $23 million. That mutual option allows either side to opt in for the final season of Pritchard's contract in 2029-30, which also opens the window for extension conversations that summer. Pritchard is currently playing on a deal that pays him $7.8 million this season and $8.3 million next year. Pritchard blossomed last season while starting 50 games, helping to ease the loss of Jayson Tatum for most of last season by taking an increased role in the offense. His touches per g…

stories.summary: Payton Pritchard, a key scoring spark for the Boston Celtics, was just rewarded after he averaged career highs in points, assists and rebounds.
stories.detail: A key piece of the revamped Boston Celtics secured his short-term future with the franchise. Guard Payton Pritchard, the 2024-25 Sixth Man of the Year, has agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension with the Celtics, with the 2029-30 season being a mutual option, according to ESPN . Messages left for Pritchard’s representatives were not immediately returned. As star forward Jayson Tatum missed much of last season, Pritchard took on more responsibility, becoming one of Boston’s primary shot makers; Pritchard averaged career highs in scoring (17.0 points per game), rebounding (3.9) and assists (5.2). Pritchard started 50 of his 79 games last season, but appears likely to resume his role as Boston’s sixth man. In the team’s preseason game against the 76ers Saturday, Oct. 10, which was something of a dress rehearsal for the Celtics, Pritchard came off the bench, before eventually leading the team with 25 points on 7-of-12 shooting. The Celtics are embarking on a new era after trading away former star Jaylen Brown to the 76ers. stories.summary: The former Sixth Man of the Year stays with the only franchise he's ever played for.
stories.detail: It's tough to envision Payton Pritchard in any uniform other than Boston Celtics green. Now, nobody will have to, at least for a few more years. The Celtics and Pritchard have agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension that keeps him in Boston, his agent told Shams Charania of ESPN . Pritchard has two more years on what is a steal of a contract ($7.2 million this season, $7.8 million in 2027-28) then he will get a massive raise starting in 2028-29 to likely $21.3 million. The deal includes a mutual option for the 2029-30 season. This is the max extension the Celtics can give Pritchard under the CBA, and it rewards his years of quality play. That said, this is a good deal for both sides. Pritchard — a key part of the 2024 championship Celtics and the 2025 Sixth Man of the Year — somewhat quietly had his best season as a pro last season, when stepping up to fill in with Jayson Tatum injured and Jrue Holiday traded. Pritchard is once again projected to come off the bench this season. Derrick White is expected to start at point guard, with Baylor Scheierman at shooting guard. stories.title: Which NBA deals will get done? Bobby Marks' biggest extension decisions to watch
stories.summary: With Monday's extension deadline looming, Bobby Marks breaks down the biggest decisions around the league.
stories.detail: The NBA season starts in one week, but that isn't the only thing on the minds of league executives. The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday, a day before the 2026-27 regular season tips off. Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama , Amen and Ausar Thompson , Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. That's currently far below the average of 11 rookie extensions signed per year since 2023, but expect that number to rise in the coming days. Of the 34 players to land rookie extensions in the past three seasons, 17 signed on deadline day. What deals will the next week bring? We broke down what to expect for six of the 16 eligible players. Rookie extension decisions aren't the only things we're watching. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans with two years remaining on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the deadline to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. Let's examine the league's most important extension decisions and what Monday's deadline could bring for teams around the league.
